line.comment: * Task 0.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Optimized shared sector queue and hostile ship detection.
* Retains the existing Explorer movement, avoidance, and homebound escape behavior.
* Queue coordination and avoidance behavior are derived from Mayhem FoF.
* "Cartographer".
* We create a special array to handle explorer sync, for performance purposes. See Mayhem.GetExplorers.
* Initialized here because the main loop reads variables assigned in subroutines.
* MSCI may otherwise report them as unassigned during compilation.
* The sector this ship has taken from the homebase list and not yet put a satellite in.
* Zero Hour: hard difficulty allows Explorers to claim empty sectors
* Zero Hour: hard and insane difficulty allow Explorers to claim empty sectors
* ZH 1.8: only 2% chance for such opportunistic claims
* ZH 2.0: reduced further to 0.2% but its no longer limited to the earlygame
* Add-Ons 1.3: Chance increased to 1% on insane.
* Sector is Unknown
* once there we need to check again because we didn't already claim on departure like Battlegroups do
* Mordan9
* 70% hull is already significant damage taken (at least 20% slower than usual).
* Any slower may risk losing the worker, so go back home to repair.
* If the factory was destroyed or the explorer was reassigned, restart immediately.
* Same homebase, has no eligible sector.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Resolve a completed attack interrupt.
* The original mapping movement may resume after FleeHome inside !ship.signal.attacked finishes.
* Do not map the sector in which the attack occurred.
* The sector may have changed owner, blacklist status, or satellite coverage during travel.
* From FoF: 2026-08-20 The satellite goes down the moment the ship arrives.
* Drop a satellite and set it to be owned by the player if this is the NPC doing us a favor.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Distinguish actual fire from hostile combat-capable ships.
* Under fire: return home. Hostile presence alone: select another mapping target.
* Nobody has fired: keep the remaining satellites and take the next target instead of flying
* home and dumping them. CheckAvoid: keeps this sector off the list for the next 30 minutes.
* Player: wait 1-2 minutes. This is an exception to the parity rule, because NPCs do not lose satellites to periodic removal.
* Therefore, they do not need to work as often as player explorers. NPCs wait 10x longer.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Evaluate combat capability instead of relative speed. This is because slower enemies in OOS can still kill.
* $underAttack means an actionable threat exists; leave this sector.
* $underFire means the Explorer was attacked; return home.
* Hostile armed presence alone sets $underAttack but not $underFire.
* Actual attacks take priority over proactive threat classification.
* OOS combat can threaten the Explorer without a conventional pursuit.
* Find hostile ships, then check whether they have usable armament.
* Freighters are excluded from proactive avoidance; actual attacks still count.
* Compatible missiles count only when actually present in cargo.
* End enemy check.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Preserve 2.2's response to actual attacks versus hostile presence.
* Actual fire sends the ship home; hostile presence alone permits continued mapping.
* Avoidance state remains per-ship and does not modify global routing.
* Half an hour of playing time, then the sector is fair game again -- long enough that the explorer
* gets useful work done elsewhere in the meantime, short enough that a garrison the player has
* since cleared out does not stay off the map forever. The entry is removed as it expires, so the
* table cannot grow without bound.
* Whether $sector still wants a satellite from this owner. It is asked when the list is built and
* again as each sector is taken, because the list can be minutes old by then.
* For the AI, we manage sector blacklist here.
* already handled by Zero Hour Core AI update
* No second satellite where we already have one.
* Only one explorer rebuilds the list at a time, because a second rebuild would put back sectors
* already taken. The marker counts only while its ship still exists and is still exploring.
* As such, one left by a destroyed or reassigned explorer is cleared.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Cache the Explorer list once per rebuild, reducing redundant lookups.
* The queue excludes destinations reserved by other Explorers at this homebase.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Spread sector checks across frames with shorter rebuild latency.
* Ignore destroyed or invalid Explorer references.
* A reassigned Explorer must not reserve a sector for this homebase.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Record when this homebase last received a completed queue.
* Always release our rebuild lock, including after reassignment.
* The homebase list of sectors waiting for a satellite, shared by every explorer based there.
* A sector leaves the list in the same instant it is taken, so no two explorers are sent to the same
* one, and the list is rebuilt only once it is empty. Returns $sector, or null when nothing is left that this ship may take.
* The homebase may have changed while we waited.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Do not rebuild an empty shared queue repeatedly.
* Preserve the existing one-rebuild-per-selection guard.
* Throttle empty-queue rebuilds across all explorers sharing this homebase.
* 2 minutes because player explorers wait up to 2 minutes, so we want to discover newly available sectors reasonably quickly.
* The queue is empty and the refresh interval has expired.
* The nearest sector to where this ship is now, passing over any it was recently driven out of.
* Zero jumps is the shortest possible distance.
* No queued sector is currently eligible because of avoidance cooldowns.
* The queue contains sectors, but none are currently eligible for this explorer.
* Avoid repeatedly rebuilding the shared queue while avoidance cooldowns are active.
* Throttle repeated rebuilds of a nonempty queue to once every 5 minutes. This allows newly eligible sectors to be discovered periodically.
* Note: this is a tradeoff with newly eligible sectors taking up to 5 minutes to enter the nonempty, all-avoided queue.
* The shared queue is old enough to refresh for newly available sectors.
* Off the list and onto this ship with no wait in between, so no other explorer can take it.
* A sector that has gained a satellite or turned hostile since the list was built is dropped,
* and the next nearest taken instead.
* $t = [THIS] + ' in ' + [SECTOR] + ' has stopped working.'
